homotopy_shortest_paths — DRIVE braidpath op

• Data kinds: image2d × any × any → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.homotopy_shortest_paths(grid, start, goal, k=4, obstacles=None, angle=0.1, max_states=400000, max_cost=None) (to call the implementation directly, import braidpath; braidpath.homotopy_shortest_paths(grid, start, goal, k=4, obstacles=None, angle=0.1, max_states=400000, max_cost=None); from the registry, opsdrive.get("homotopy_shortest_paths"))

Usage

On a grid (True = traversable, 4-neighbourhood), the k shortest paths from start to goal in distinct homotopy classes, shortest first.

State = (cell, Dynnikov coordinates of the braid). Obstacle points are treated as stationary strands; each move appends the crossing letter and updates the coordinates (the coordinates are a complete invariant of the class, so each (cell, coordinates) is expanded only once). Dijkstra expands this “class-lifted” grid in order of cost, so the order in which goal is reached with new coordinates is the shortest-first order of the per-class shortest paths.

Parameters

obstacles : representative points of holes (M, 2). If omitted, grid_hole_points (one point per blocked component not touching the border).

max_states / max_cost : upper bounds on the number of expanded states and on the cost (there are infinitely many classes —— a hole can be circled any number of times).

Returns: dict paths (each class's (L, 2) sequence of (row, col), shortest first), costs, words (braid words including the obstacles), keys, obstacles, states (number of expanded states), complete (whether all k paths were found).
